observations: Imagery under the weather picture: the USGS tiles show under the radar or forecast picture, the town bubbles, the NWS outlines and the credit row. The Montana outline and the state and country borders stay visible as pale lines.

USGS draws its own place names and region names in the raster (for example MONTANA, IDAHO, Yellowstone National Park, Bighorn River, Boise). They sit beside our town bubbles. The builder saw a second Helena name beside its bubble at about zoom 8; this check did not look for double names.
ImageryTopo carries USGS contour lines with elevation numbers at high zoom (seen at zoom 16 on a rural spot). The contract's units text does not mention contours.
The outside-area hatch (faint diagonal lines) still draws over the imagery outside the picture's box, so the Outside map area key still matches the map.

Portrait phone legend: with imagery on, the credit row makes the legend taller: 181 px at 390 px wide (151 px without), 196 at 375 (165), 228 at 320 (182), 343 at 288 (283). DESIGN.md gives 135 to 170 px for the portrait legend; the new figure is recorded there.
Layers menu: the Map and Imagery rows have no swatch, so their labels sit 36 px left of the weather labels. It reads fine; a spacer would align them.
Tiles refused (every request aborted): the white paper background, borders and bubbles remain, there is no banner and no script error, and the credit row still shows.
Dark mode: the imagery is shown in natural colour (no filter); only the page chrome changes.
No sideways scroll at 288, 320, 375, 390, 768 or 1440 px, in the default state and with imagery on (scroll width equals client width in every case).

Corrected in this stage (2026-10-18): the brief's statement that zoom 9 and up outside the United States return 404 is wrong for most of Canada. At zoom 9, Calgary, Lethbridge and Regina return a blank white 200 tile (2,419 bytes, every pixel 255). Toronto returns a near-white one (2,767 bytes; 99.7% of pixels at 250 or more), and Vancouver a mostly white one (8,197 bytes; about 91% at 250 or more). Paris, Sydney and Tokyo return 404. DECISIONS D32 and DESIGN.md now say so. Measured by fetching the tiles and decoding them (imagery-work/fix/tiles-check/stats.json).

Corrected in this stage (2026-10-18): the ImageryTopo facts are in labels-on-globe.json and montana-imagery-buildings.json, not base-imagery.json (which covers the ImageryOnly service). The measured tile sizes are 15.7 to 35.7 KB: 15.7 to 32.3 KB at zoom 7 in the fit view (35 tiles), and 35.5 KB (Billings) and 35.7 KB (Missoula) at zoom 16. The 23 to 38 KB range in labels-on-globe.json is a summary note with no listed measurement, so D32 no longer uses 38 KB.

Tiles refused: the credit row still reads 'Imagery: USDA, USGS, The National Map' while no imagery is drawn, and nothing says so. This follows the design (no banner), but a reader can take the white map for a failed imagery layer. A short line is the suggested follow-up (see the owner decisions).

Corrected in this stage (2026-10-18): the earlier builder's report that on a short landscape phone the credit row is hidden until the info button opens the legend is wrong. At 667x375, 740x360 and 844x390 with imagery on, the credit row starts below the visible legend (363 px at 667x375). The info button only shows the legend note, which pushes the credit lower (430 px). The legend column scrolls (213 px visible of 291 px at 667x375), and after scrolling it the credit row is in view (284 to 313 px). The credit is reached by scrolling the legend, not by the info button (imagery-work/fix/probe-landscape.json).

Failed tiles (review, 2026-10-18): with every imagery request aborted, the map shows a near-white background, the Montana outline, the state and country lines and the 10 town bubbles, and no base-map land, lakes, rivers, roads, counties or names (0 shapes, 0 names). The credit row still shows and no banner appears. The brief's wording ('leaves the white map showing underneath') was wrong; sources.py, DESIGN.md and D32 now say what happens, and smoke_map check_imagery_refused tests it (imagery-work/fix/probe-refused-before.json, refused-before.png).

Request headers (review, 2026-10-18; imagery-work/fix/probe-headers.json): a tile request sends an Origin header (the page's origin) and a Referer that holds the origin only (http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ on the local test server; that is what the browser's default referrer policy sends for a request to another site), the browser's User-Agent and client hints, and no cookies. The review's first note, that the Referer held the full page address, was wrong. Stage E re-checks the headers on the final build. The privacy line names none of these; D32 records them and leaves the wording to the owner.

Link behaviour (review, 2026-10-18; imagery-work/fix/probe-direct.json): map.html?base=imagery made 35 requests to the imagery host while the page opened, with no click, and was on Imagery when the probe read it, 8 seconds after the page opened. The privacy line is inside the closed Layers menu, so it is not seen on arrival. D32, DESIGN.md and the About page say a link can switch Imagery on. Stage E: the credit row with the privacy words is on the page from the start (see the stage E observations).

Layers menu on a 667x375 phone (review; imagery-work/fix/probe-menu.json): the menu box is 56 to 363 px and scrolls (305 px visible, 487 px tall). The Imagery label starts at 356 px, and only its top 7 px fit above the menu's bottom edge at 363 px, so it needs a scroll on first view. At 1280x800 it is in view (312 to 389 px).

Leftover tile layer (review): with the removeLayer call deleted from setBase, switching back to Map kept one tile layer and 35 imagery pictures on the page, and the browser check still passed. The check now asserts after each switch back that the layer and its pictures are gone (tools/smoke_map.py imagery_gone); the good build has none (imagery-work/fix/probe-mut-m4.json, probe-good.json).

The base commit used wait_until='load' in this check (line 317 of the base file), and the held precipitation pictures keep that event open, which timed the check out under load (the fix stage's full runs). The wrapper now names the check that could not run.

Stage E correction (2026-10-18): a tile request's Referer holds the page's origin only. imagery-work/stage-e/probe-e-on.json on the final storm build: origin 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT', Referer 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT/' for a page at map.html; no cookie header; the user-agent and sec-ch-ua hints are sent. The stage D statement that the Referer holds the full page address was wrong and is corrected above.

Stage E correction (2026-10-18): the base map's roads, lakes, rivers, counties and names stay hidden for as long as Imagery is on (the #app.is-imagery rules in map.css have no tile condition). The earlier wording 'until a tile loads' was wrong; sources.py, DESIGN.md and D32 now say 'while Imagery is on'.

owner_decisions: Licence: whether to accept USGS's public-domain statement for the road and name data on ImageryTopo (open in rights-matrix.json).
Outage behaviour: an answer from USGS that is not 200 image/jpeg fails the branch smoke step, while no answer at all is only a note. Say if an outage should be a note too.
Bubble names on imagery: whether the town bubbles' names should be hidden while imagery is on, because USGS draws its own names.
Contract wording: whether the imagery contract should mention the contour lines.
Privacy line: add that the tile request also carries the page's origin and the browser's User-Agent? D32 records both.

Phone legend height with imagery: the privacy sentence in the credit row makes the legend 210 px at 390 px wide (151 px without imagery) and 400 px at 288 px (283 px without). Shorten the credit on small screens, or accept? Also whether the Map and Imagery rows should align with the weather labels.

Failure words: while every tile fails, the failure words replace the credit row, so the privacy sentence is off the row (the requests were still sent; the Layers menu and About keep the sentence). Keep the words as the supervisor specified, or add the sentence to the failure line?
